title: A Comprehensive Survey of Multi-Agent Systems Through a Layered Taxonomy Spanning Science, Engineering, and Applications
content: Multi-agent systems have emerged as a dominant architectural paradigm for applied AI, yet deploying them effectively requires bridging scientific understanding of agent coordination with engineering constraints and real-world application demands. This survey presents a unified perspective on the multi-agent AI landscape, synthesizing research across the science of how multiple LLM-driven agents coordinate, the engineering of systems that implement that coordination under production constraints, and the application-level evidence of where such systems deliver measurable value. We introduce a layered taxonomy of multi-agent capabilities, spanning Agent Primitives, Coordination, Communication, Intelligence, and Assurance. We then organize 13 functionalities into 8 key concepts derived inductively from the literature, situated within the layered taxonomy of multi-agent capabilities: (Agent specialization, Orchestration patterns, Decision making, Context engineering, Learning, Evaluation, Tracing & Monitoring, and Security & Safety). For each concept, we trace its intellectual origins, survey current scientific findings, examine engineering design patterns, and ground the discussion in enterprise deployments. We motivate multi-agent architectures through an analysis of single-agent limitations (including context saturation, instruction-following degradation, tool selection noise, and limited modularity) while acknowledging that multi-agent decomposition is not universally superior and introduces its own coordination overhead. We identify principled criteria for when multi-agent coordination is justified over single-agent designs, and examine the responsible AI mechanisms necessary for trustworthy operation at scale. We conclude by outlining directions for future research on open challenges, including evaluation difficulty, cost efficiency, emergent security threats, and governance in a rapidly shifting regulatory landscape.
